title: Copenhagen cryptogram (Schmeh Top 50 no. 23), slip found behind an 1835 portrait of a Danish general

steps.what: Transcribed the scan (20-symbol merged reading) and collated ShadowWolf's 25-symbol reading.
Symbol counts; o only after n, 'non' twice, digits 4 and 5 absent.
Simple-substitution annealing in ten languages under six reading conventions, both transcriptions.
Dotted strokes as word separators, scored with a spaced model.
103-letter enciphered passages: 12 of 15 recovered at 40 restarts; true text scores -1.4 to -2.1 per letter.
300-restart reruns on the strongest languages; ceiling -2.8 per letter, no better.

outcome.method_basis: Simple-substitution annealing in ten languages under several reading conventions produced nothing readable, while matched controls of the same length were solved.
outcome.notes: Closed from the only scan; needs the original slip, the painting's identity, or a non-substitution model.

prior.where: Schmeh's Cipherbrain posts and comments; Matthew Brown's Danish hill-climb also failed

human: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
